question: When viewed as matrices, which flags of African nations have the same linear algebraic rank as the flag of Denmark? Assume that values in each matrix are chosen so that the rank of each flag is maximal.

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Benin, Madagascar, and Guinea-Bissau. Denmark’s stripe/cross layout has maximal rank 2: after partitioning into row and column blocks, it has only two independent row profiles, namely the central white band and the red-white-red flanking bands. The African flags that match this are those with a full-height hoist stripe and a fly split into two stacked rectangles, giving a 2×2 block matrix of the form [[a,b],[a,c]], whose rank is 2 when the values are chosen generically. Benin and Madagascar clearly have this structure. Guinea-Bissau also has the same block structure; its black star is contained within the hoist stripe, so under a maximal assignment it changes the value assigned to that stripe but does not add a new independent row/column direction. Thus the matching flags are Benin, Madagascar, and Guinea-Bissau.

17.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Benin, Guinea-Bissau, and Madagascar.

Denmark’s flag, in its natural rectangular partition, gives a matrix of the form

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
R & W & R\\
W & W & W\\
R & W & R
\end{pmatrix},
\]

whose maximal rank is \(2\). So we need African flags whose maximal rank is also \(2\).

Benin and Madagascar both reduce to the same two-independent-row pattern: a full-height hoist stripe plus two horizontal fly bands, e.g.

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b\\
a & c
\end{pmatrix},
\]

which has maximal rank \(2\).

Guinea-Bissau has the same basic structure as Benin: a full-height red hoist stripe with yellow and green fly bands. Its black star lies inside the red hoist stripe, so when the color matrix is reduced it contributes only within that hoist column and does not create a third independent row or column beyond the hoist/fly split. Hence its maximal rank remains \(2\).

So the African flags with the same maximal rank as Denmark are Benin, Guinea-Bissau, and Madagascar.

Its color-block matrix is essentially a 2-rank cross pattern, and the African flags with the same maximal rank are those whose major color fields form a vertical stripe plus a two-part right side. That gives **Benin, Madagascar, and Guinea-Bissau**. Benin is green | yellow/red, Madagascar is white | red/green, and Guinea-Bissau is red | yellow/green; each yields a matrix of the form \([a\ c;\ a\ d]\) with \(a(c-d)\neq 0\), so the maximal rank is 2. The black star on Guinea-Bissau lies inside the red stripe and does not change the rank of the underlying stripe-block matrix once values are chosen maximally.

Guinea-Bissau also has that same structure—red vertical band on the hoist and yellow/green horizontal split in the fly.
